note: Five members: brolucizumab approved 2019, conbercept approved in China but failed global phase 3, abicipar refused for inflammation, NT-503 stopped on rescues, RGX-314 in phase 3; no admissible model source found for NT-503 or RGX-314.
label: AMD (anti-VEGF-A binders)

engagement.confidence_note: Sponsor report TDOC-0013037 dated January 2011, unpublished; read in the FDA review (2019).
engagement.judgement: Opened at the sponsor report date (2011), the model's first documented use; the data became public only in the 2019 review.
engagement.note: Intravitreal brolucizumab shrank laser-induced CNV lesions in mice by 17-35%, without a clear dose response.
engagement.quote: Brolucizumab exhibited activity for decreasing CNV lesion size compared to vehicle.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Registry results posted 2019-10-31 (NCT02307682, NCT02434328).
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: mouse CNV area against human CST/fluid, both downstream of VEGF-A neutralisation. Direction only; the FDA reviewer doubted the model reached target saturation.
engagement.note: HAWK/HARRIER: brolucizumab reduced central subfield thickness and retinal fluid more than aflibercept, as CNV suppression in mice predicted.
engagement.quote: Anatomic retinal fluid outcomes favored brolucizumab over aflibercept.

engagement.model: Rat subretinal/suprachoroidal RGX-314 with VEGF-induced vascular leakage
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. First-use year is the first public date; the rat work likely predates the 2017 phase 1 start.
engagement.note: In rats, subretinal or suprachoroidal RGX-314 expressed anti-VEGF Fab and suppressed VEGF-induced leakage.
engagement.quote: Compared with subretinal injection in rats of RGX-314, an AAV8 vector expressing an anti-VEGF Fab, suprachoroidal injection of the same dose of RGX-314 resulted in similar expression of anti-VEGF Fab and similar suppression of VEGF-induced vascular leakage.

engagement.model: Rat subretinal/suprachoroidal RGX-314 with VEGF-induced vascular leakage
engagement.magnitude_basis: RGX-314 Fab protein in ocular fluid
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; registry results (2023-05-16) do not report aqueous protein, so year is the Lancet epub.

engagement.judgement: Paired, not stated. Ding 2019 appeared after phase 1 dosing began (2017) but before protein data were published; treated as prospective (retrodiction false), low risk because transgene expression is not tuned to patient results.

dose.confidence_note: IND-enabling study supported the first-in-human trial C-10-083 (~2011); unpublished until the 2019 review.
dose.judgement: Year is a proxy for the IND-enabling study and first-in-human trial.
dose.note: Monkey intravitreal studies set an ocular NOAEL of 6 mg/eye, a 2-fold vitreal-concentration margin over the 6 mg human dose.
dose.quote: The high-dose of 6 mg/eye was established as the ocular no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL).

dose.magnitude_basis: monkey NOAEL 3 mg/ml vitreous vs human 1.5 mg/ml at 6 mg/eye
dose.confidence_note: Full FDA pharmacology/toxicology review read in the bundle (Table 39: 2-fold margin on a mg/ml basis).
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the monkeys never showed intraocular inflammation, so the harm is a safety miss, not a misplaced margin; counted once, in safety. Dose scored same with margin_stated.
dose.note: Patients were dosed at the 6 mg/eye regimen the monkey margin supported; the unpredicted inflammation is scored in safety.
dose.quote: The results of this study support chronic dosing of patients with brolucizumab.
dose.reason: Clinical dose reached within stated margin

dose.confidence_note: Year is a proxy (rabbit PD study BIO-12-960 and toxicology before the 2015 phase 3); data public only in the 2020 EMA report.
dose.note: Repeat intravitreal abicipar caused intraocular inflammation in rabbits; ocular NOAEL 1 mg/eye, about 3 mg/eye human-equivalent, above the 2 mg dose.
dose.quote: In rabbits abicipar administered as 3 injections at 2-month interval resulted in an ocular NOAEL of 1 mg/eye which corresponds to approximately 3 mg/eye in humans.

dose.magnitude_basis: rabbit ocular NOAEL human-equivalent (3 mg/eye) vs dose with 15% IOI (2 mg/eye)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level for the trial paper; model side from EMA withdrawal assessment report EMA/415176/2020, which calls the ocular margins 'quite low'. Registry results posted 2020-07-28 (NCT02462928).

Scored blocked_by toxicity because the regimen could not be registered, although patients were dosed to target; efficacy is still scored on its own track.
dose.note: At 2 mg/eye, below the rabbit NOAEL equivalent, 15.4% of patients had intraocular inflammation versus 0.3% on ranibizumab; EMA application withdrawn, FDA refused.
dose.quote: Incidence of intraocular inflammation (IOI) AEs was 15.4%, 15.3%, and 0.3%, respectively.

dose.quote: Thus, predictions for human PK by multi-compartment PK model support dose selection and treatment regimen of 2 mg/eye 2Q8/2Q12.

dose.model: Mechanistic multi-compartment ocular PK model, rabbit-scaled to human (abicipar)

dose.reason: fit to patient PK used in scaling
dose.judgement: Scored retro, not same: the human model was scaled using patient aqueous and serum data, so its fit is a retrodiction.

efficacy.note: PHOENIX: conbercept gained 9.20 letters versus 2.02 on sham at month 3, the primary endpoint.

efficacy.judgement: Efficacy scored as the trial showed even though the dose entry is contra: patients were dosed to target and the endpoint was met; the inflammation is counted in dose.
